alt: Rayang holding the finished soft underwater robot prototype at UCL
title: Bio-Inspired Pneumatic Soft Actuators for Underwater Robots
p: Soft silicone limbs modelled on manta rays and trilobites, pumped with water so a robot can explore coral reefs without harming them.

alt: The finished 3D-printed prosthetic hand, palm side
title: Constructing and Analysing the Performance of a Modified Prosthetic Hand
p: A low-cost, 3D-printed five-finger hand that closes when you flex your forearm muscles.

alt: Freshly printed black InMoov parts laid out on a cutting mat beside a craft knife
title: Rebuilding the InMoov robot hand
p: Printing and assembling Gaël Langevin’s open-source InMoov hand, from the first print to the first movement.

alt: Simulation replay: a glowing cloud of fruit-fly neurons inside a see-through fly head
title: A fly’s brain when it tastes sugar?
p: The published whole-brain model of the fruit fly, fed sugar and followed spike by spike, then run again with two neurons silenced.

alt: Screen recording of Gesture Music: both hands make signs, the camera view labels the notes and the matching pads light up
title: Gesture Music, an instrument you play with hand signs
p: A webcam watches both hands and each sign plays a note, a chord or a drum, with a looper, live MIDI, a rhythm game and a 62-page handbook.

alt: My printed TARS standing on a desk
title: Building my own TARS
p: The robot from Interstellar, printed and assembled from the TARS-AI community’s open build kit, then taught seven new moves in a physics simulation.

alt: The web HMI of the T-101 batch station during HOLD
title: A batch tank with no cook
p: A heated mixing tank run by a PLC program in Structured Text, proven against a virtual plant with 66 automated tests, then run on OpenPLC v4.

alt: The GH-1 operator HMI overview with the water tank, dosing pumps and four drip zones
title: GH-1 Tropical Greenhouse
p: A PLC program for a 1,000 m² tropical greenhouse, tested end to end against a virtual plant, and playable in your browser.
meta: 130 tests · play it in your browser

alt: A map of the Riemann zeta function in deep blue and violet, with its first ten zeros glowing gold on one straight line
title: Proved, Checked, Not Yet Understood. Claude and the Riemann Hypothesis
p: An Anthropic mathematician says he proved the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude. Lean certified it in a day. Nobody can yet explain why it is true.

alt: The gold plated cover of the Voyager Golden Record against black
title: A Day Away. Voyager 1 Is Now One Light Day from Home
p: Voyager 1 is the first spacecraft a full light day from Earth, so a radio hello now takes a day each way. How it got there, what it found and what it still carries.

alt: A man in a blue polo shirt making the time out sign with his hands
title: Skin in the Game. Why Noise Can Help Light Pile Up at One Edge
p: Lossy steps push light towards one edge. Scrambling its phase can speed that drift up, and damping kills or boosts it depending on when it acts.

alt: A man typing furiously at a keyboard with a big grin
title: Practice Makes Plastic. Brain Cells After One Typing Lesson
p: A finger tapping lesson made brain cell bodies swell for a while and cell branches grow denser by the next day, seen in living people with an ultra strong MRI.

alt: Three papercraft cats, folded from flat sheets, sitting on a tiled floor
title: Folded Twice, Moves Eight Ways. A Bistable Origami Robot
p: A 0.81 g origami robot with two stable shapes: small magnetic nudges make it crawl or roll, one big pulse snaps it shut.
